_comment: pairs_app: do stocks that move together pay to trade against each other? Two ideas, on daily bars only, with the same development / validation / holdout years as config/morning.json and the same pass marks. Rules are fixed here BEFORE the first run (2026-11-14); nothing is tuned by it.
_universe_comment: Each month, from the formation_days trading days before it: the universe_size stocks with the most dollar volume, priced above min_price, with a bar every day. Only stocks averaging at least prefilter_dollar_volume a day over the morning screen's daily bars (data/morning/daily) are downloaded, when those exist.
_pairs_comment: Pairs trading, the distance method (Gatev, Goetzmann, Rouwenhorst 2006). Each month: the `pairs` pairs whose prices (each divided by its first price) tracked closest over the last formation_days (smallest sum of squared differences; no stock in two pairs). Then for trading_days: when the gap between them is more than open_sigma times its formation standard deviation, short the one above and buy the one below, equal dollars; close when the gap closes (the prices cross) or the window ends. delay_days 1 opens and closes a day after the signal, as published. The control: random pairs from the same universe.
_lead_lag_comment: Lead-lag: each month, each stock's leader is the bigger stock (more dollar volume) whose daily returns moved most with its own over formation_days, if the correlation is at least min_correlation. Each day, buy the stocks_each_side stocks whose leader beat them most today and short those it trailed most, at the close, held hold_days. The control: a random bigger stock as leader.
_money_comment: Positions held overnight: at most leverage x equity in all, shared equally between everything that can be open at once. Costs as everywhere else: slippage_percent against us on each fill, regulatory fees on sells. A short's borrowing cost isn't counted.
